front: BC ground search and rescue tasks in 2022?
back: 1,510 tasks; 1,019 lives saved (95%, BCSARA 2022 review).

front: Biggest activity slice of BC ground SAR tasks, 2022?
back: Hiking, about 41%. Hunting has no slice of its own (80%, my reading of the chart).

front: Does BC charge you for a search and rescue?
back: No. "You don't pay to be rescued" (95%, BCSARA report); NSR: no cost for rescue (75%).

front: BCSARA top 10 worst things: name 4 about planning and navigation.
back: No trip plan; only a cell phone and maybe water; no "what if"; not knowing your location (95%).

front: BCSARA's number 1 worst thing?
back: Wrong footwear: slips, trips, falls, broken bones (95%).

front: How do hunters usually get lost?
back: Following an animal or a blood trail intently through dense brush (65%, Koester via Popular Science).

front: What does FACETS stand for?
back: Familiarity, Acceptance, Consistency, Expert halo, Tracks or scarcity, Social facilitation: six thinking traps from avalanche accidents (80%).

front: "One more ridge, we came this far." Which trap?
back: Consistency: committed to a goal as things get worse (80% for the trap; Tip for the example).

front: "Last day, last hour of light." Which trap?
back: Scarcity (tracks): racing a closing window (80%; example Tip).

front: 7 lines of a trip plan?
back: Who; vehicle and plate; where parked with coordinates; route A and B; back by; call 911 if; gear and colours (75% core, Tip extras).

front: When should you call 911 if lost or hurt?
back: As soon as you know. Dial 911, ask for police (75%, North Shore Rescue).

front: Who activates ground SAR in BC?
back: Agencies such as police, BC Ambulance, fire services. You call 911 (95%, BCSARA).

front: Box yourself in: the 3 kinds of lines?
back: Baseline you can always walk back to; handrails on the sides; a backstop you never cross (Tip, built on orienteering, 85%).

front: What is a handrail?
back: A line feature you can follow without the compass: creek, road, fence, power line, timber edge, ridge (85%, Little Book of Orienteering).

front: What is a catching feature?
back: A big line just past your target that tells you that you overshot (85%).

front: What is an attack point?
back: A big, easy feature near the target. Go big, then go small (85%).

front: What is a collecting feature?
back: Something you pass on the way that tells you that you are on track, like a creek you cross (85%).

front: Escape bearing?
back: The rough bearing that always reaches your baseline, e.g. road to the south: about 180. Write it on your hand (Tip).

front: First two things at the truck?
back: Drop a Parking waypoint and note the escape bearing (99% app; Tip).

front: Why look back at every fork?
back: The way out looks different from the way in (Tip).

front: How often should you find yourself on the map?
back: Every 15 to 30 minutes; more often in timber, fog, snow and dark (Tip).

front: Walking speed off trail and on a road?
back: About 4 km/h off trail, 5 on roads (75%, Aitken). Add 1 h per 600 m of climb (75%, Naismith).

front: The first sign you are unsure. What do you do?
back: Stop. Go back to your last sure point if you can see it or follow your track. Otherwise full STOP (Tip; 75%).

front: 1:50,000: what is 1 cm on the ground?
back: 500 m. So 2 cm is 1 km (99%, maths).

front: 1:20,000: what is 1 cm?
NTS standard map scales?
Contour gap 1 mm, 20 m lines, 1:50,000: how steep?
back: About 22 degrees. 2 mm about 11; 0.5 mm about 39 (95%, my calculation).

front: Hunt Map contour interval?
back: 20 m, with a thicker index line every 100 m (99%, app). Feet mode: 40 and 200 ft.

front: Contours cross a creek in a V. Which way does it point?
back: Upstream, toward higher ground (95%, USGS).

front: Ridge versus draw on contours?
back: Ridge: bends point downhill. Draw: bends point uphill (85%).

front: Contour lines touching or merging mean?
back: A cliff (95%).

front: Topo map colours: brown, blue, green?
back: Brown contours; blue water and grid; green vegetation (95%, USGS). Read each sheet's legend.

front: How do you read a UTM grid reference?
back: Right first (easting), then up (northing) (95%).

front: UTM zones: Heffley Creek, Mission, Osoyoos?
back: Heffley Creek and Mission zone 10; Osoyoos zone 11 (90%).

front: Declination at Heffley Creek, Oct 2026?
back: 15.17 degrees east, changing minus 0.13 a year (95%, NOAA World Magnetic Model).

front: Declination at Mission and Osoyoos?
back: Mission 15.20 E; Osoyoos area 14.58 E (95%, NOAA).

front: Grid north near Heffley Creek?
back: About 2.5 degrees east of true north, so the needle is about 12.7 degrees east of grid lines (85%, my calculation).

front: Declination east, magnetic ...?
back: Least: map to compass subtract 15; compass to map add 15 (90%).

front: Four compass jobs?
back: Take a bearing, follow it, reverse it (back bearing), find yourself (cross bearings).

front: Taking a map bearing: what about the needle?
back: Ignore it on the map. Ring lines to map north lines (95%).

front: Following a bearing: where are your eyes?
back: On a target tree on the line, not on the needle (95%).

front: Two person leapfrog?
back: Brother walks ahead; you wave him onto the line; walk to him; repeat. Stay in sight (Tip).

front: Back bearing of 40? Of 300?
back: 220 and 120. Under 180 add 180, over 180 take 180 (95%).

front: Best angle between two landmarks for a cross bearing?
back: About 90 degrees (85%).

front: On a road, one landmark. How do you find where you are?
back: Take a bearing to it; where its back bearing crosses the road is you (Tip, from resection, 85%).

front: Why aim off?
back: So you know which way to turn when you hit the road or shore (85%).

front: How much to aim off at 2 km?
back: More than your error: 5 degrees is about 175 m, so 200 to 300 m (98% maths; Tip).

front: Miss per km for 1 degree of error?
back: About 17 m (98%).

front: Forgot declination near Kamloops: miss per km?
back: About 268 m (98%). Set it west instead: 577 m.

front: Three things that bend the needle?
back: Steel (rifle, truck), magnets, phones and electronics (80%). Step away.

front: How do you orient a map with the compass?
back: Turn the map, not yourself, until its north lines run with the needle (95%).

front: Orient a map with no compass?
back: Line up a road, ridge or lake on the map with the real one; check a second feature (95%; Tip).

front: Thumb the map?
back: Thumb beside your position; move it as you walk (Tip, orienteering habit).

front: Terrain association in 4 steps?
back: Name 3 big features; find them on the map; check their order; mark where you must be (Tip).

front: One feature doesn't fit. What does it mean?
back: You are probably not where you think. Don't bend the map (Tip).

front: Where am I? The order to try?
back: Handrail plus one bearing; landforms; cross bearings; phone checked on paper; else STOP and stay (Tip).

front: Mid October sunrise and sunset bearings at Heffley Creek?
back: Rise about 103 degrees, set about 257 (85%, my calculation).

front: When is the sun due south at Heffley Creek in mid October?
back: About 12:46 daylight time, 30 degrees up (85%).

front: Shadow stick: which mark is west?
back: The first mark. Rough check only (60%).

front: BC clocks in November 2026?
back: No fall back: BC stays on daylight time (95%, BC government release, via Weather and daylight).

front: Does phone GPS need cell signal?
back: No (95%). Map tiles do: save Offline Maps at home.

front: Three Offline Maps choices in the Hunt Map?
back: My base area (Heffley Creek, about 25 km), This view, Draw a box (99%, app).

front: Offline Maps: what is NOT saved?
back: Satellite photos (99%, app).

front: What does Back to start show?
back: Distance and heading to where you started recording, e.g. 1.9 km, 214 degrees (SW); green dot = start (99%, app).

front: Hunt Map track: when are points skipped?
back: When GPS accuracy is worse than 30 m: "GPS is weak" (99%, app code).

front: Typical phone GPS accuracy in the open?
back: About 4.9 m (16 ft); worse near trees and cliffs (90%, gps.gov).

front: Why can't the Hunt Map track with the screen off on iPhone?
back: iPhone web apps cannot record with the screen off; the app keeps the screen awake (99%).

front: No track, only a truck pin. Heading to the truck?
back: Tools, Draw and measure, Measure from your dot to the pin (99% tool; Tip use).

front: iPhone operating temperature range?
back: 0 to 35°C. Colder, it may shut off; it recovers when warm (95%).

front: iPhone satellite SOS needs?
back: iPhone 14 or later, iOS 16.1 in Canada, no cell or wifi, clear view of sky and horizon (95%).

front: Satellite messenger versus PLB?
back: Messenger: two way text, paid plan (65%). PLB: one way SOS on 406 MHz, no plan for SOS (60%).

front: Phone died in the cold. First?
back: STOP, then warm it inside your jacket about 15 minutes (95% Apple: recovers when warm).

front: STOP stands for?
back: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan (75%, AdventureSmart).

front: AdventureSmart on moving when lost?
back: "It's always harder for search teams to find you if you move" (75%).

front: First 10 minutes when lost?
back: 0 to 3 sit, drink, eat; 3 to 6 think: last sure point; 6 to 10 observe; then plan (Tip).

front: When does moving make sense?
back: Sure of the way back in daylight; fresh tracks in snow; or your spot is dangerous (Tip). Any doubt: stay (75%).

front: Double the distance you wander. Search area?
back: 4 times bigger (95%, geometry).

front: Which way do lost hunters drift?
back: Downhill and off trail (65%, Koester).

front: Why not follow a creek downhill?
back: Ravines are steep, unstable and hard to escape (75%, North Shore Rescue).

front: What do you say first on a 911 call when lost?
back: Where: coordinates and their format. Then who, what, what you have, your plan (Tip).

front: Distress signals?
back: Three of anything: whistle, mirror, light, fires. Ground V or SOS at least 3 m (75%).

front: Aiming a mirror with no sight?
back: Two fingers in a V on the target; tilt the light onto the V; flash in threes (Tip).

front: You hear a searcher's whistle?
back: Three blasts back and stay put. Answer every call (70%).

front: Night out order?
back: Safe spot; insulate from the ground; roof; fire if safe and legal; signal, water, food (Tip).

front: When to decide to stay out?
back: About 1 hour before dark (Tip).

front: Pick the spot: bench or bottom?
back: Bench. Cold air drains into low ground at night (75%).

front: Roof or bed first?
back: Bed: the ground pulls heat by conduction (75%).

front: Category 1 campfire size?
back: No bigger than 0.5 m high by 0.5 m wide; 8 L of water or a hand tool on hand; check bans (80%).

front: Wet tinder that still burns?
back: Birch bark and pitch wood (65%).

front: Boil water how long?
back: At least 1 minute; above 2,000 m at least 2 (80%, HealthLink BC).

front: Early hypothermia signs?
back: Stumbles, mumbles, fumbles, grumbles (75%).

front: Shivering stops and drowsy?
back: Moderate hypothermia: gentle, horizontal, wrap, warm the trunk, get help (75%).

front: AdventureSmart's 10 essentials?
back: Light, fire kit, signal, extra food and water, extra clothes, navigation and communication, first aid, shelter, knife, sun protection (75%).

front: Legal light end for big game?
back: 1 hour after sunset (99%, Rule Book). Mid Oct Heffley Creek: about 19:08 (85%).

front: Hunt Map red slopes?
back: 30 to 45 degrees: avalanche terrain in snow (99% app; 95% Avalanche Canada).

front: Clear blue ice to walk alone?
back: At least 15 cm; 20 for a group (75%, Canadian Red Cross).
About 1 minute cold shock, 10 minutes useful movement, 1 hour to unconscious (80%).

front: PFD law in a boat?
back: An approved PFD of the right size on board for each person; inflatables worn in open boats (99%).

front: ATV deaths in BC?
back: Almost 13 a year on average; about half rollovers (60%, CBC).

front: Rifle on the ATV?
back: Unloaded: nothing in the chamber or an attached magazine (98 to 99%).

front: Bear or cougar: run?
back: Never (75%). Moose: run and put a tree between you (85%).

front: Zone of fire for two hunters?
back: About 45 degrees straight ahead each; middle and behind are no shot (75%).

front: Turnaround time formula?
back: At truck time, minus the walk out, minus about 30 minutes buffer (Tip).

front: Compass triangle drill pass mark?
back: Finish within about 10 m of the start on 3 legs of 100 m (Tip).

front: Map vs land drill pass mark?
back: 3 of 5 pencil dots within about 200 m (Tip).

front: Phone drill: 3 rounds?
back: Back to start; pin only with Measure; phone dead pretend with escape bearing (Tip).

front: Lost scenario drill pass mark?
back: STOP, fix or stay decision, signal and shelter within 30 minutes (Tip).

front: Practise the 911 call in a drill?
back: Say the script, coordinates first. Do not dial (Tip).
